verses.pali: “Pañcime, bhikkhave, ādīnavā dīghacārikaṁ anavatthacārikaṁ anuyuttassa viharato.
verses.english: “Mendicants, there are these five drawbacks for someone who likes long and aimless wandering.

verses.pali: Assutaṁ na suṇāti, sutaṁ na pariyodāpeti, sutenekaccena avisārado hoti, gāḷhaṁ rogātaṅkaṁ phusati, na ca mittavā hoti.
verses.english: You don’t learn new things. You don’t clarify what you’ve learned. You lack confidence in some things you have learned. You contract a severe illness. You don’t have any friends.

verses.pali: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ādīnavā dīghacārikaṁ anavatthacārikaṁ anuyuttassa viharato.
verses.english: These are the five drawbacks for someone who likes long and aimless wandering.
There are these five benefits of a reasonable amount of wandering.

verses.pali: Assutaṁ suṇāti, sutaṁ pariyodāpeti, sutenekaccena visārado hoti, na gāḷhaṁ rogātaṅkaṁ phusati, mittavā ca hoti.
verses.english: You learn new things. You clarify what you’ve learned. You have confidence in some things you have learned. You don’t contract severe illness. You have friends.

verses.pali: Ime kho, bhikkhave, pañca ānisaṁsā samavatthacāre”ti.
verses.english: These are the five benefits of a reasonable amount of wandering.”
